note: E4/F3: an id this server instance does not hold: 404, in three cases (SPEC section 5): not admitted yet (the window before its admission), never admitted (an HTTP-level 400 or the expired 409; or never received), or ended and dropped by time or count (past its retention). The service treats it as unresolved (no re-ask) when server_instance is the one it dispatched to. server_time_ms (F3) is the server's clock, read in the critical section of the lookup that found nothing: when it is strictly greater than a request's not_after_ms, no request with this id and that not_after_ms is admitted on this server_instance after the lookup (section 5). A real run of the F3 binary: the service lost a /resolve with this request_id and not_after_ms 1794065251000 (never received here); this 404 states 1794065252566, past it, and the request sent after it was refused 409 expired (server_time_ms 1794065252568). Engines before F3 omit the field: a client then has no proof from the 404.
